paper_title: A Spectral Approach to Scalable Vectorless Thermal Integrity Verification

scenario.description: Two microprocessor designs (Processor A and B) used for experimental validation of the spectral vectorless thermal integrity verification method. Processor A has 28W power consumption, 195 mm² die area, 4 metal layers, 11 material layers. Processor B has 50W power consumption, 302 mm² die area, 6 metal layers, 15 material layers. Both use equivalent heat transfer coefficients of 3.3×10³ W/m²K for heat sink and 2.0×10³ W/m²K for package.
scenario.architecture: 3D thermal grid based on microprocessor die with metal and material layers; heat transfer modeled through package and heat sink with equivalent thermal conductance coefficients
scenario.workload: Vectorless thermal analysis under local and global power density constraints without requiring exact workload vectors; worst-case temperature and thermal gradient distributions computed via linear programming optimization
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state thermal analysis; Processor A at 28W nominal power; Processor B at 50W nominal power; analysis focuses on worst-case thermal profiles under uncertain power distributions within specified constraints

original_setup.solver: Cholesky decomposition (LU factorization for thermal matrix T)
original_setup.benchmark: Two microprocessor designs (Processor A: 28W, 195mm², 4 metal layers, 11 material layers; Processor B: 50W, 302mm², 6 metal layers, 15 material layers)

thermal_observable.location: All nodes in 3D thermal grid; worst-case distributions computed across entire chip
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature and thermal gradients under worst-case power density constraints

physical_mismatches.reason: Vectorless analysis lacks specific workload vectors; relies on power density constraints rather than actual task execution traces
3D thermal grid sparsification reduces mesh fidelity; spectral approximation preserves low-frequency temperature components but may miss high-frequency spatial details
Steady-state analysis only; does not capture transient thermal dynamics or temporal power variations
Linear thermal model (linear programming formulation); assumes linear superposition of thermal effects without nonlinear feedback or temperature-dependent material properties

studio_assumptions: Thermal conductance matrix T is symmetric and diagonally dominant (M-matrix properties)
Power sources modeled as heat-generating nodes in 3D mesh with local and global constraint boundaries
Ambient thermal conductance gmin is small relative to internal resistances, enabling low-pass filtering interpretation
Heat transfer coefficients for package (2.0×10³ W/m²K) and heat sink (3.3×10³ W/m²K) are constant across operating range
Graph Laplacian eigenvalue spectrum preserves low-frequency modes after spectral sparsification; higher eigenvalues can be discarded without affecting worst-case temperature accuracy
Solution refinement via weighted Jacobi iteration (Algorithm 2) converges within specified iteration count Nmax
Multilevel hierarchy can be constructed via algebraic multigrid (AMG) restriction and prolongation operators without loss of critical constraint information
missing_inputs: Exact 3D geometry files (mesh coordinates, dimensions) for Processor A and B thermal grids
Complete thermal conductivity values for each of 11 (Processor A) and 15 (Processor B) material layers
Detailed boundary condition specifications (ambient temperature, convection correlations, radiation models)
Actual power distribution maps or power delivery network (PDN) integration details
Workload-to-power mapping functions or representative power traces for validation
Code repository or supplementary materials for Algorithm 1 (iterative edge weight scaling) and Algorithm 3 (multilevel verification framework)
Numerical values for sensitivity threshold εth and scaling factor β used in experiments
Specific LP solver configuration parameters and convergence tolerances used with Gurobi
Details on low-degree node elimination and node aggregation procedures referenced in Figure 1
Comparison baseline results or alternative vectorless thermal verification methods for relative performance assessment
